acetaminophen-vs-aspirin.text: Aspirin is the older molecule by a century and the more chemically aggressive of the two. It is acetylsalicylic acid, made by acetylating willow-bark salicylic acid in 1897, and it blocks the COX enzymes irreversibly, which is why a single exposure affects platelets for days. Acetaminophen does not do that at all: it works centrally, has little anti-inflammatory effect, and leaves clotting alone. The table shows aspirin's carboxylic acid and ester against acetaminophen's amide and phenol, which is the structural reason aspirin irritates a stomach lining and acetaminophen does not. Reported oral LD50 in rats is 200 mg/kg for aspirin against 1944 mg/kg for acetaminophen, an unusually wide gap for two drugs sold on the same shelf.

acetaminophen-vs-ibuprofen.text: These are the two painkillers most households keep, and they are not the same kind of drug. Ibuprofen is an NSAID: it blocks the COX enzymes throughout the body, which is why it reduces inflammation and swelling as well as pain. Acetaminophen, called paracetamol outside the US, acts mainly in the central nervous system and does very little for inflammation, which is why a sprain and a headache are not the same problem for it. The functional groups in the table show the split, ibuprofen carrying a carboxylic acid and acetaminophen an amide and a phenol. Their reported oral LD50 values differ by a factor of three, 1944 mg/kg in rats for acetaminophen against 636 mg/kg for ibuprofen, though the risks that actually matter for each are organ specific rather than a matter of the headline number.

acetic-acid-vs-citric-acid.text: Both are the sour in a kitchen and they behave differently because of how many acid groups each carries. Acetic acid has one carboxylic acid group and is the whole of vinegar's sourness and smell, volatile enough to fill a room. Citric acid has three, is a solid crystal, and has no smell at all, which is why lemon-flavoured products use citric acid for the sour and something else for the aroma. Those three groups also make citric acid a good chelator, binding metal ions, which is why it descales a kettle better than vinegar does. Citric acid is far heavier at 192.12 against 60.05, and it is a real intermediate in the citric acid cycle that every aerobic cell runs.

acetone-vs-ethyl-acetate.text: These are the two solvents in nail polish remover, and the choice between them is about aggression. Acetone is a small ketone that dissolves polish fast and also strips oils from skin and nail, which is the drying people notice. Ethyl acetate is an ester, heavier at 88.11 against 58.08, slower to evaporate and gentler on the nail plate, which is why it is what acetone-free removers actually contain. Ethyl acetate also smells fruity rather than sharp, and it occurs naturally in wine and ripe fruit. Both are flammable and both carry a GHS Danger signal word, so acetone-free is a statement about the solvent, not about the hazard class.

acetone-vs-isopropyl-alcohol.text: These two are one oxidation step apart: remove two hydrogens from isopropyl alcohol and you have acetone, which is exactly what the liver does to it. That is why acetone shows up on the breath after isopropyl alcohol exposure, and also why the body produces acetone on its own when it burns fat for fuel. As solvents they behave differently: acetone is a ketone and dissolves plastics, resins and nail polish that isopropyl alcohol leaves alone, which is why acetone is the aggressive one. Both are highly flammable and both carry a GHS Danger signal word. Weights are close at 58.08 and 60.1, so the difference is entirely in the functional group.

aciclovir-vs-valaciclovir.text: Valaciclovir is aciclovir with the amino acid valine attached, and the body removes that valine almost completely on first pass through the liver, so what circulates is aciclovir. The attachment exists purely to solve an absorption problem: aciclovir taken by mouth is poorly absorbed, and valaciclovir raises the amount that reaches the blood several fold. Both therefore work the same way, being activated only inside virus-infected cells by a viral enzyme and then jamming the viral DNA polymerase, which is what makes them so selective. Valaciclovir is the heavier molecule at 324.34 against 225.2 because of the added valine, and fewer doses are needed. Aciclovir's discovery won a share of the 1988 Nobel Prize in Medicine.

adenosine-vs-caffeine.text: These two are not alternatives, they are opponents, and that is the whole reason the pair is interesting. Adenosine is a molecule your body makes continuously while you are awake, and as it accumulates and settles onto its receptors, you feel more and more like sleeping. Caffeine happens to fit those same receptors closely enough to occupy them without switching them on, so the sleepiness signal keeps being sent and stops being heard. Nothing is added by the coffee: the alertness is the absence of a message. When the caffeine clears, the adenosine that piled up in the meantime is still there and lands all at once, which is what an afternoon crash actually is. Their structures show the family resemblance, both purines, adenosine carrying a whole ribose sugar that caffeine lacks.

agar-vs-gelatin.text: Agar is the plant answer to gelatin and it does not behave the same way. Agar is a polysaccharide from red seaweed; gelatin is hydrolysed animal collagen, a protein. Agar sets much firmer, holds at room temperature, and only melts around 85 degrees Celsius, which is why it is the standard medium for growing bacteria in a warm incubator where gelatin would liquefy. Gelatin melts near body temperature, which is precisely why it feels the way it does in the mouth and agar does not. Agar also sets at a much lower concentration for the same firmness. For a vegetarian or vegan recipe, agar is the substitute, but it is not a like for like swap in texture.

alprazolam-vs-diazepam.text: Both are benzodiazepines and both work by making the brain's own GABA more effective at its receptor, and the difference between them is timing. Alprazolam acts fast and clears fast, with a half-life around 11 hours, which is why it is associated with acute panic and also with a sharper rebound as it leaves. Diazepam is absorbed very quickly but persists far longer, and it produces long-lived active metabolites including nordazepam that can stretch its effect over days. That is why diazepam is used to taper other benzodiazepines and alprazolam is not. Alprazolam is the more potent per unit weight by a wide margin. Structurally alprazolam carries a triazole ring fused to the benzodiazepine core that diazepam lacks.

amitriptyline-vs-nortriptyline.text: Nortriptyline is amitriptyline with one methyl group removed, and the body performs exactly that conversion, so taking amitriptyline produces nortriptyline as an active metabolite. Both are tricyclic antidepressants that block serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake, and the missing methyl shifts the balance: nortriptyline leans more toward norepinephrine and carries fewer antihistamine and anticholinergic effects. That is why nortriptyline is generally the less sedating of the two and causes less dry mouth and constipation. Both are used at low levels for nerve pain and migraine prevention as well as for depression. Weights differ by the methyl group alone, 277.4 against 263.4.

amlodipine-vs-lisinopril.text: Both are first-line blood pressure medicines and they act on completely different systems. Amlodipine is a calcium channel blocker: it stops calcium entering the smooth muscle of artery walls, so the vessels relax directly. Lisinopril is an ACE inhibitor and works hormonally, reducing the production of angiotensin II. Their characteristic side effects follow from the mechanisms: amlodipine causes ankle swelling by dilating arterioles more than venules, and lisinopril causes a dry cough through bradykinin accumulation. Because the two routes are independent, they are often combined rather than substituted. Amlodipine is the heavier at 408.9 against 405.5 and carries two chlorine-bearing rings.

ammonia-vs-sodium-hypochlorite.text: This pair matters for one reason: mixing them is a well-known way to make a toxic gas at home. Sodium hypochlorite in water releases hypochlorous acid, and hypochlorous acid reacts with ammonia to form chloramines, which irritate the airways badly and can be dangerous in an enclosed room. Both are common household cleaners in their own right, bleach for whitening and disinfecting and ammonia for glass and grease, and both carry a GHS Danger signal word on their own. Ammonia is the far smaller molecule at 17.03 against 74.44 and is a gas dissolved in water rather than a salt. The reason many cleaning products warn against mixing is this reaction specifically.

amoxicillin-vs-azithromycin.text: Both are common antibiotics and they belong to different classes with different targets. Amoxicillin is a penicillin: it carries the four-membered beta-lactam ring that blocks bacterial cell wall construction, which is why it is inactivated by beta-lactamase enzymes and why it is often paired with clavulanic acid. Azithromycin is a macrolide, a large 15-membered ring that binds the bacterial ribosome and stops protein synthesis. Azithromycin accumulates inside tissue and clears very slowly, which is why a short course keeps working for days after the last dose, while amoxicillin clears in hours and must be taken repeatedly. Azithromycin is far the larger molecule at 749.0 against 365.4. Penicillin allergy is the usual reason a prescriber reaches for one class over the other.

aripiprazole-vs-risperidone.text: Both are atypical antipsychotics and they treat the dopamine receptor in opposite ways. Risperidone is a straightforward D2 blocker with strong 5-HT2A blocking added, so at higher amounts it behaves much like an older antipsychotic, including a marked rise in prolactin. Aripiprazole is a partial agonist: it occupies the same receptor and produces a low level of activation, damping signalling where dopamine is high and supporting it where dopamine is low. That mechanism is why aripiprazole tends to be more activating and less prolactin raising, while risperidone is the more sedating. Aripiprazole is the heavier of the two at 448.4 against 410.5.

aspartame-vs-saccharin.text: Saccharin is the older sweetener by a century, discovered in 1879, and it is the simpler molecule: a small sulfur-containing ring at 183.19 against aspartame's 294.3. Saccharin is also the sweeter of the two, roughly 300 times sugar against 200, and it is the one with the metallic aftertaste that shows up at higher concentrations. Aspartame breaks down with heat and cannot be baked with; saccharin is stable and can. The reported oral LD50 for saccharin is 14200 mg/kg in rats, which is very high, and much of saccharin's reputation traces to a 1970s rat bladder study whose mechanism turned out not to apply to people. Aspartame's constraint is different and specific: it delivers phenylalanine.

aspirin-vs-ibuprofen.text: Both are NSAIDs that work by blocking COX enzymes, and both carry a carboxylic acid on an aromatic ring, so they are far closer relatives than either is to acetaminophen. The difference is reversibility. Aspirin acetylates the enzyme permanently, so its effect on platelets outlives the molecule in the blood, which is the basis of its use in cardiology. Ibuprofen binds and lets go, so its effect fades as it clears, with a half-life near 2 hours. Ibuprofen is also the more potent anti-inflammatory at the doses people actually use, and it is the newer molecule by seventy years. Reported oral LD50 in rats is 200 mg/kg for aspirin and 636 mg/kg for ibuprofen.

atorvastatin-vs-rosuvastatin.text: Both are statins that block HMG-CoA reductase, the rate-limiting enzyme in the body's own cholesterol assembly line, and rosuvastatin is the more potent per unit weight. The larger practical difference is how each is cleared: atorvastatin is broken down by the liver enzyme CYP3A4, which is the enzyme grapefruit juice and many other medicines interfere with, and rosuvastatin is largely not, so it has fewer interactions. Rosuvastatin is also more water-loving, which keeps more of it in the liver where it is meant to act. Atorvastatin became the best-selling medicine of all time as Lipitor; rosuvastatin followed as Crestor. Atorvastatin is the heavier at 558.6 against 481.5, and rosuvastatin carries a sulfonamide group that atorvastatin does not.

benzene-vs-toluene.text: Toluene is benzene with a methyl group attached, C7H8 against C6H6, and that single group changes the hazard picture completely. Benzene is a known human carcinogen that damages bone marrow and causes leukaemia, and its use in consumer products is tightly restricted for that reason. Toluene is not classified as a carcinogen, because the body can oxidise that methyl group and excrete the result, a route benzene has no equivalent of. Toluene is still a neurotoxin on repeated inhalation, which is what makes solvent abuse dangerous, and it is the smell of paint thinner and permanent marker. Reported oral LD50 values are 3306 mg/kg in rats for benzene and 5000 mg/kg for toluene, which understates how differently the two behave over long exposure.

beta-carotene-vs-retinol.text: Beta-carotene is essentially two molecules of retinol joined tail to tail, which the body can cut in the gut wall to make vitamin A. That conversion is the entire difference. Retinol is preformed vitamin A from animal sources and is used directly, so it accumulates and can reach toxic levels; beta-carotene is converted only as needed, so surplus is stored in fat and skin rather than causing vitamin A toxicity. Eating a very large amount of beta-carotene turns skin orange, which is harmless and reversible. Beta-carotene is the orange of carrots and sweet potato and is nearly twice retinol's weight at 536.9 against 286.5. Conversion efficiency varies a great deal between people.

borax-vs-sodium-bicarbonate.text: Both are white powders sold in the laundry aisle and they are not interchangeable. Sodium bicarbonate is a simple sodium salt of carbonic acid, mildly alkaline, edible, and used as much in baking as in cleaning. Borax is sodium tetraborate, a boron compound, more strongly alkaline, and not edible: boron compounds carry reproductive-toxicity classifications in the EU and borax is restricted in consumer products there. Borax is the better water softener and stain remover of the two because of that higher alkalinity, and bicarbonate is the better deodoriser because it neutralises acids directly. Their weights are far apart, 201.2 for the anhydrous borax on record against 84.01.

bupropion-vs-sertraline.text: These two are both antidepressants and they work on entirely different neurotransmitters. Sertraline is an SSRI and acts on serotonin; bupropion acts on dopamine and norepinephrine reuptake and leaves serotonin essentially alone. That difference drives most of what separates them in practice: bupropion does not carry the sexual side effects or the weight gain associated with SSRIs, and it is activating rather than calming, while it does lower the seizure threshold in a way SSRIs do not. Bupropion is also sold under a second name as a smoking cessation aid, which sertraline is not. Bupropion is much the smaller molecule at 239.74 against 306.2.

butane-vs-propane.text: Both are alkanes sold as bottled fuel and the difference is one carbon and one temperature. Propane boils at about minus 42 degrees Celsius and butane at about minus 1, which means propane stays a usable gas in cold weather and butane will not vaporise properly near freezing. That is the whole reason a winter camping stove takes propane and a lighter takes butane. Butane is the heavier at 58.12 against 44.1 and liquefies under gentler pressure, which is why it can be held in a thin clear lighter body while propane needs a steel cylinder. Butane delivers slightly more energy per unit volume as a liquid, and propane more per unit weight.

caffeine-vs-theanine.text: These two arrive together in tea and are usually discussed as an offsetting pair. Caffeine is an alkaloid that blocks adenosine receptors and produces alertness. Theanine is an amino acid found almost nowhere but the tea plant, structurally close to glutamate, and it appears to raise alpha wave activity and take the edge off caffeine's jitteriness without cancelling the alertness. That combination is the usual explanation for why a cup of green tea feels different from a coffee of similar caffeine content. They are unrelated molecules, C8H10N4O2 against C7H14N2O3, and theanine is the lighter at 174.2. Theanine has no reported stimulant effect on its own.

caffeine-vs-theobromine.text: Caffeine and theobromine are the same molecular skeleton with one difference: caffeine carries three methyl groups where theobromine carries two, which is the whole of the C8H10N4O2 against C7H8N4O2 in the table. That one group changes how strongly each binds the brain's adenosine receptors, and caffeine binds far harder, which is why coffee arrives as a jolt and chocolate does not. Theobromine lingers longer instead, with a half-life around 7.2 hours against caffeine's 5, so cocoa's lift is slower and flatter. Both come from the same plants in different proportions: coffee and tea lead with caffeine, cocoa leads with theobromine. The reported oral LD50 also splits them, 192 mg/kg in rats for caffeine against 300 mg/kg in dogs for theobromine, and it is theobromine that dogs clear too slowly to tolerate.

caffeine-vs-theophylline.text: Theophylline is caffeine minus one methyl group, C7H8N4O2 against C8H10N4O2, and the two sit in the same alkaloid family for that reason. Both block adenosine, but theophylline also relaxes airway muscle strongly enough that it was used as an asthma medicine for most of the twentieth century, which caffeine never was. It stays in the body longer, a half-life near 8 hours against caffeine's 5. Tea carries both, with caffeine dominant and theophylline in traces, so a cup does not deliver a medicinal amount of either. Their reported oral LD50 values are close, 192 mg/kg in rats for caffeine and 332 mg/kg in mice for theophylline, which is a reminder that the gap between the two is about what they do rather than about how toxic they are.

cannabidiol-vs-cannabigerol.text: Cannabigerol is the precursor that the cannabis plant builds most of its other cannabinoids from, including cannabidiol, which is why mature plants contain very little of it. Both are non-intoxicating and neither activates the CB1 receptor the way THC does. Their structures are close: CBG keeps a straight, open chain where CBD has closed a ring, and CBG carries two more hydrogens, 316.5 against 314.5. Because CBG is consumed by the plant's own synthesis, extracting it commercially means harvesting early or using selectively bred low-conversion strains, which is why CBG products cost more. The research base behind CBG is far thinner than CBD's.

capsaicin-vs-piperine.text: Both are the heat in a spice and they act on the same receptor with very different force. Capsaicin from chilli and piperine from black pepper both activate TRPV1, the nerve channel that reports heat and physical damage, which is why both feel like burning even though nothing is hot. Capsaicin is far the stronger, at roughly 16,000,000 Scoville units in pure form against piperine's 100,000, a difference of over a hundredfold. They also differ in the character of the heat: capsaicin builds and lingers, and piperine bites sharply and fades. Structurally capsaicin carries a long fatty tail on a vanillyl amide, and piperine is a compact ring system, which is why capsaicin is the more fat-soluble and harder to wash out with water.

celecoxib-vs-ibuprofen.text: Both are NSAIDs, but they aim at different halves of the same enzyme family. Ibuprofen blocks COX-1 and COX-2 more or less equally; celecoxib was designed to hit COX-2 while largely sparing COX-1, which is the enzyme that maintains the stomach lining and normal platelet function. That selectivity is the entire reason celecoxib exists, and it shows in the structure: a sulfonamide and a trifluoromethyl group on a pyrazole core, nothing like ibuprofen's small propionic acid. Celecoxib is prescription only and ibuprofen is sold over the counter, which is the most visible difference to a shopper. It is also nearly twice the weight, 381.4 against 206.28.

cholecalciferol-vs-ergocalciferol.text: These are vitamin D3 and D2 and they differ in a side chain, C27H44O against C28H44O. D3 is what human skin makes when ultraviolet B light hits 7-dehydrocholesterol, and it is also what comes from fish and lanolin. D2 is the fungal and plant version, made when the same light hits ergosterol, which is why ultraviolet-treated mushrooms are sold as vitamin D enhanced. Both are converted by the liver and kidney into the active hormone, but D3 raises and holds blood levels of the storage form more effectively than D2 does, which is the practical reason most supplements now use D3. D2 remains the vegan option and the historical form used to fortify milk.

cholesterol-vs-testosterone.text: Testosterone is built from cholesterol, so this is a precursor and its product rather than two competing molecules. Cholesterol is the four-ring sterol every animal cell membrane uses to control its fluidity, and the body makes most of its own rather than absorbing it from food. From cholesterol the adrenal glands and gonads build pregnenolone and from there the whole steroid hormone family, testosterone included, along with cortisol, estradiol and vitamin D. The visible difference is size: cholesterol keeps a long hydrocarbon tail and weighs 386.7, and testosterone has lost that tail at 288.4. The common belief that eating cholesterol raises testosterone does not follow from the pathway, which is not limited by the supply of raw material.

citric-acid-vs-ascorbic-acid.text: These two are often confused because both are sour, both come from citrus, and both are used as preservatives, but only one is a vitamin. Ascorbic acid is vitamin C, which humans cannot make and must eat; citric acid is not a vitamin at all and the body produces it constantly as part of the citric acid cycle. Citric acid preserves by lowering pH, while ascorbic acid preserves by being oxidised in place of the food, which is why it stops cut apples browning. Their weights are close, 192.12 and 176.12, and both are white crystalline powders, which is part of why the labels get misread. A product listing citric acid is making no claim about vitamin C.

clonazepam-vs-alprazolam.text: Both are high-potency benzodiazepines with a triazolo or nitro group that sets them apart from the older members of the class, and both act on the same GABA-A receptor. Clonazepam lasts substantially longer, with a half-life in the range of 30 to 40 hours against alprazolam's 11, which is why it is used for seizure disorders and long-acting anxiety control where alprazolam is used for acute episodes. The shorter action of alprazolam is also why it is the more associated with between-dose rebound. Both are controlled substances in the US and in most of Europe. Clonazepam carries a nitro group and a chlorine at 315.7; alprazolam has the triazole ring at 308.8.

codeine-vs-tramadol.text: Both are weak opioids that owe much of their effect to being converted by the liver into something stronger, which is the most interesting thing they share. Codeine is a natural poppy alkaloid, morphine with a methyl group on one oxygen, and the enzyme CYP2D6 strips that group to make morphine. Tramadol is fully synthetic and unrelated in shape, and the same enzyme turns it into a metabolite with far more opioid activity than the parent. In both cases a person's version of that enzyme decides how much drug they are actually getting, which is a real source of variation between people. Tramadol adds serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake blocking that codeine does not have, so the two are not simply different strengths of the same idea.

collagen-vs-gelatin.text: Gelatin is collagen that has been cooked, and that is the entire relationship. Collagen is the structural protein of skin, tendon and bone, three chains wound into a rigid triple helix that gives tissue its tensile strength. Heat in water unwinds that helix irreversibly, and the loose chains that result are gelatin, which is why simmering a bone broth thickens it as it cools. Collagen supplements are generally hydrolysed further into short peptides, so what is sold as collagen powder is closer to gelatin than to the intact protein. Neither reaches the skin as collagen after being eaten: both are digested into amino acids like any other protein.

collagen-vs-keratin.text: These are the two structural proteins most people have heard of, and they build different things by different means. Collagen is a triple helix that gives skin, tendon and bone their tensile strength, and it is rich in glycine and proline. Keratin is a coiled coil packed with cysteine, and the sulfur bridges between those cysteines are what make hair, nail, horn and hoof hard and insoluble. That disulfide bonding is why hair can be permanently waved by breaking and reforming those bridges, and why burning hair smells of sulfur. Collagen dissolves into gelatin when cooked; keratin does not dissolve at all, which is why hair survives in archaeological finds.

cortisol-vs-epinephrine.text: These are the two stress hormones, and they run on different clocks. Adrenaline is released within seconds by the adrenal medulla and clears within minutes, producing the immediate racing heart and widened pupils of an acute fright. Cortisol is a steroid built from cholesterol, released over minutes to hours by the adrenal cortex, and it changes how the body handles glucose, immunity and inflammation for the rest of the day. Cortisol also follows a daily rhythm on its own, peaking shortly after waking, which adrenaline does not. Structurally they have nothing in common: cortisol is a four-ring steroid at 362.5, adrenaline a small catecholamine at 183.2.

creatine-vs-creatinine.text: These are constantly mixed up and one is simply the waste product of the other. Creatine is stored in muscle as phosphocreatine, a rapid phosphate reserve that regenerates ATP in the first seconds of hard effort, which is what makes it useful as a sports supplement. Creatinine is what creatine becomes when that molecule spontaneously cyclises and loses water, at a fairly constant rate proportional to muscle mass. The kidneys clear creatinine, so its level in blood is a standard measure of kidney function, and that is why a creatine supplement can raise a measured creatinine reading without anything being wrong with the kidneys. The weights differ by exactly the lost water, 131.13 against 113.12.

curcumin-vs-piperine.text: These two are usually named together because piperine is added to turmeric supplements to make curcumin usable. Curcumin is the yellow pigment of turmeric, poorly absorbed and rapidly conjugated by the liver and gut wall, so very little of what is swallowed reaches the bloodstream intact. Piperine, the sharp compound in black pepper, inhibits some of the enzymes that perform that conjugation, which is why the two are formulated together. They are otherwise unrelated: curcumin is a phenolic diketone at 368.4 and piperine an alkaloid at 285.34, and piperine carries heat that curcumin does not. Curcumin is also a pH indicator that turns red in alkali, which is what stains a wooden spoon.

diazepam-vs-lorazepam.text: Both are benzodiazepines and the useful distinction is what the liver has to do with them. Diazepam is broken down through oxidation into several active metabolites, so its effect outlasts the parent molecule and accumulates with repeated use, especially in older people and in anyone with reduced liver function. Lorazepam is conjugated directly and produces no active metabolite, so its effect ends more cleanly, which is why it is often preferred where liver function is a concern. Diazepam is the more fat-soluble of the two and reaches the brain faster, which matters when either is used for an acute seizure. Lorazepam is the heavier at 321.2 against 284.7.

diphenhydramine-vs-cetirizine.text: These are the first and second generation antihistamines, and the difference is whether the molecule reaches the brain. Both block the H1 histamine receptor, which is what stops the itching and sneezing of an allergic response. Diphenhydramine is small and fat-soluble enough to cross the blood-brain barrier freely, which is why it causes strong drowsiness and why it is sold as a sleep aid as well as an allergy medicine. Cetirizine carries a carboxylic acid that keeps it largely out of the brain, so it is much less sedating while blocking the same receptor in the body. Cetirizine also lasts far longer, which is why it is a once-daily product and diphenhydramine is not.

donepezil-vs-memantine.text: Both are used in Alzheimer's disease and they act on opposite sides of the synapse. Donepezil blocks acetylcholinesterase, so the acetylcholine that is still being released lasts longer, which is a way of making the most of a declining supply. Memantine blocks the NMDA glutamate receptor partially, which is aimed at the excess glutamate signalling thought to damage neurons in later disease. Because the two mechanisms do not overlap, they are frequently used together rather than as alternatives. Donepezil is the larger molecule at 379.5 against memantine's 179.3, and memantine is an adamantane, the same cage structure as the antiviral amantadine.

dopamine-vs-norepinephrine.text: Norepinephrine is made from dopamine by a single enzyme adding one hydroxyl group, so this pair is a molecule and its immediate product, C8H11NO2 against C8H11NO3. The body runs the chain tyrosine to L-dopa to dopamine to norepinephrine to adrenaline, and each step is one small modification. Functionally they diverge: dopamine dominates in reward, motivation and movement circuits, and norepinephrine drives arousal, attention and the fight-or-flight response, and acts as a hormone as well as a neurotransmitter. Several medicines act on both at once, which is why stimulant drug descriptions usually name the pair together. The reported oral LD50 for norepinephrine is 20 mg/kg in mice, which makes it one of the more acutely toxic entries in this catalog.

doxycycline-vs-azithromycin.text: Both stop bacteria making protein and they bind different parts of the ribosome. Doxycycline is a tetracycline and blocks the 30S subunit; azithromycin is a macrolide and blocks the 50S. Both penetrate tissue well and both cover the atypical organisms that cell-wall antibiotics miss, which is why they overlap in respiratory and sexually transmitted infections. Doxycycline causes photosensitivity and stains developing teeth, which is why it is avoided in young children, and azithromycin does not. Azithromycin is the much larger molecule at 749.0 against 444.4, and its very long tissue half-life is why courses are short.

duloxetine-vs-venlafaxine.text: Both are SNRIs, blocking the reuptake of serotonin and norepinephrine rather than serotonin alone, and they weight the two differently. Venlafaxine is strongly serotonergic at lower amounts and only recruits norepinephrine as the amount rises, so its character changes across its range. Duloxetine hits both from the start, which is part of why it is used for nerve pain and fibromyalgia as well as for depression. Venlafaxine has a notably short half-life and produces a well-known discontinuation syndrome when stopped abruptly; duloxetine is somewhat gentler on that front. Structurally duloxetine carries a thiophene ring and a naphthalene ether at 297.4, and venlafaxine is a simpler phenol ether at 277.4.

epinephrine-vs-norepinephrine.text: One methyl group separates them, C9H13NO3 against C8H11NO3, and the enzyme that adds it works mostly in the adrenal medulla. That is the cleanest way to think about the pair: norepinephrine is the version the nervous system releases at nerve endings, and adrenaline is the version the adrenal gland pours into the blood as a hormone. They also favour different receptors. Norepinephrine acts mainly on alpha receptors, tightening blood vessels and raising blood pressure, while adrenaline hits beta receptors strongly too, which is what opens the airways and is the reason an adrenaline injector works for anaphylaxis. Both are naturally occurring and both carry a GHS Danger signal word in this catalog.

erythritol-vs-allulose.text: These are both sugar substitutes that behave almost like sugar in the mouth but not in the body, and they belong to different chemical classes. Erythritol is a sugar alcohol, C4H10O4, absorbed and excreted essentially unchanged. Allulose is a real sugar, a rare epimer of fructose with the same C6H12O6 formula as glucose, which the body absorbs but barely metabolises. That distinction matters in the kitchen: allulose browns and caramelises the way sugar does because it is one, and erythritol does not. Erythritol has the cooling mouthfeel that sugar alcohols share, while allulose does not, and allulose is the less sweet of the two at roughly 70 percent of sugar.

escitalopram-vs-citalopram.text: Citalopram is a mixture of two mirror-image forms of the same molecule and escitalopram is the active one isolated. The inactive half does not simply sit there: it appears to blunt the active half slightly, which is the argument for separating them. Everything else is identical, same formula C20H21FN2O, same weight of 324.4, same serotonin transporter. Half the amount of escitalopram does roughly what a full amount of citalopram does, which is why the numbers on the two prescriptions look different for what is chemically the same substance. Citalopram carries a stronger warning about heart rhythm at higher amounts than escitalopram does.

estradiol-vs-progesterone.text: Both are steroid hormones central to the menstrual cycle and they act in sequence rather than in competition. Estradiol dominates the first half of the cycle, building the uterine lining, and progesterone dominates the second half after ovulation, maintaining it. Structurally estradiol is the more modified: its first ring is aromatic and carries a phenol, which is what makes it an estrogen, while progesterone keeps the intact steroid skeleton with two ketones and is the direct precursor of cortisol and testosterone. Progesterone is the heavier at 314.5 against 272.4. Both are made from cholesterol, and both appear here as body-endogenous molecules rather than as medicines.

estradiol-vs-testosterone.text: These are the two headline sex hormones and one is made from the other. The enzyme aromatase converts testosterone into estradiol by aromatising the first ring, which is visible in the table: estradiol carries a phenol group and testosterone a ketone, and estradiol has lost a carbon at 272.4 against 288.4. Everyone makes both. Testosterone predominates in men and drives muscle, bone density and body hair; estradiol predominates in women and drives the menstrual cycle, and it is also essential to bone health in men, through exactly that aromatase conversion. Both are steroids built from cholesterol, four fused rings apiece.

ethanol-vs-isopropyl-alcohol.text: Both are alcohols and both disinfect, and only one is a drink. Isopropyl alcohol has one more carbon and branches, C3H8O against C2H6O, and the body oxidises it to acetone rather than to acetic acid, which is why swallowing it causes a very different and more dangerous picture than drinking ethanol. As a disinfectant, 70 percent solutions of either outperform higher concentrations, because some water is needed for the alcohol to get through a cell wall before it denatures the proteins inside. Isopropyl alcohol evaporates leaving less residue, which is why it is the one used on electronics. The reported oral LD50 values are 5628 mg/kg in rats for ethanol and 4797 mg/kg in dogs for isopropyl alcohol.

ethanol-vs-methanol.text: One carbon separates them, C2H6O against CH4O, and that single carbon is the difference between an intoxicant and a poison. The body oxidises both with the same enzymes. Ethanol becomes acetaldehyde and then acetic acid, which the body handles routinely. Methanol becomes formaldehyde and then formic acid, which attacks the optic nerve and drives the acidosis that makes methanol poisoning dangerous. The listed oral LD50 values are similar, both near 5628 mg/kg in rats, which is exactly why the LD50 is a poor guide here: the danger is what the metabolites do, not the parent molecule. Methanol is present in tiny amounts in fermented drinks and is the reason improperly distilled spirits are hazardous.

ethylene-glycol-vs-propylene-glycol.text: These two differ by one carbon and the difference is toxicological rather than chemical. Ethylene glycol is C2H6O2 and the body oxidises it to oxalic acid, which forms calcium oxalate crystals in the kidneys, and that is what makes antifreeze poisoning so damaging. Propylene glycol is C3H8O2 and is metabolised to lactic acid, which the body handles routinely, which is why it is permitted in food, e-liquid, and medicines. Both are sweet tasting, and the sweetness of ethylene glycol is a recurring hazard to pets and children. Many antifreeze products now use propylene glycol for exactly that reason, and some add a bitterant to the ethylene glycol kind.

famotidine-vs-omeprazole.text: Both reduce stomach acid and they act at different points in the same machinery. Famotidine is an H2 blocker: it blocks the histamine receptor on the acid-producing cell, which turns the signal down and works within an hour. Omeprazole is a proton pump inhibitor: it permanently disables the pump that actually moves acid into the stomach, so it takes days of repeated use to reach full effect but reduces acid far more completely. That is why one is useful for occasional heartburn and the other for sustained reduction. Omeprazole needs an acidic environment to activate, which is why its capsules are coated to survive until they are absorbed. Famotidine is the smaller molecule at 337.5 against 345.4 and contains sulfur in two places.

finasteride-vs-minoxidil.text: Both are used for male pattern hair loss and they attack it from different directions. Finasteride blocks 5 alpha reductase, the enzyme that converts testosterone into dihydrotestosterone, and DHT is what miniaturises the follicle, so finasteride addresses the cause. Minoxidil does nothing to hormones at all: it was a blood pressure medicine whose side effect was hair growth, and applied to the scalp it widens vessels and appears to lengthen the growth phase of the follicle. Finasteride is a prescription steroid-like molecule taken by mouth at 372.5; minoxidil is sold over the counter as a topical liquid or foam at 209.25. Because the mechanisms do not overlap they are commonly used together.

formaldehyde-vs-acetaldehyde.text: Both are small aldehydes, both are reactive, and both are classified as carcinogenic to humans, but they arrive by different routes. Formaldehyde is the simplest of all aldehydes at 30.03, used in resins, embalming fluid and disinfectants, and it cross-links proteins on contact, which is precisely what preservation and what irritation both are. Acetaldehyde at 44.05 is what ethanol becomes as the body breaks it down, and it is responsible for much of a hangover and for the flushing reaction in people whose version of the clearing enzyme works slowly. Their reported oral LD50 values differ by more than sixfold, 100 mg/kg in rats for formaldehyde against 661 mg/kg for acetaldehyde. The body produces both in small amounts as a normal part of metabolism.

gabapentin-vs-pregabalin.text: Both are built on the skeleton of GABA, the brain's main inhibitory neurotransmitter, and neither actually acts on the GABA receptor. Both bind the alpha-2-delta subunit of voltage gated calcium channels instead, reducing the release of excitatory neurotransmitters, which is how they work in nerve pain and in some seizure types. The practical difference is absorption: gabapentin is taken up by a saturable transporter, so absorption falls as the amount rises and the response is hard to predict, while pregabalin is absorbed proportionally and predictably. Pregabalin is the smaller molecule at 159.23 against 171.24 and is a controlled substance in the US and the UK where gabapentin's status varies. Gabapentin's reported oral LD50 is 8000 mg/kg in rats.

gelatin-vs-pectin.text: Both set a liquid into a gel and they come from opposite kingdoms. Gelatin is collagen from animal hide and bone, broken down into protein chains that tangle as they cool, which is why a gelatin gel melts at body temperature and feels like it dissolves in the mouth. Pectin is a plant polysaccharide from fruit peel and needs sugar and acid to set, giving a firmer gel that holds its shape at room temperature. That is the whole reason jam uses pectin and dessert jelly uses gelatin. Pectin is the only option of the two for a vegetarian product. Gelatin sets on cooling and can be re-melted; a pectin gel is effectively set for good.

glucose-vs-fructose.text: They have the identical formula, C6H12O6, and the identical weight, and they are still different molecules: glucose closes into a six-membered ring and fructose into a five-membered one, with a ketone where glucose has an aldehyde. That difference decides where each goes. Nearly every cell in the body can burn glucose directly, and blood sugar means glucose specifically, while fructose is handled almost entirely by the liver. Fructose is the sweeter of the two by a wide margin, which is why fruit tastes sweeter than its sugar content alone suggests. Table sugar is one of each joined together, and high-fructose corn syrup is the same two sugars unjoined and slightly rebalanced.

glucose-vs-glycogen.text: Glycogen is not a different sugar, it is thousands of glucose units branched together, which is why its listed formula and weight represent a fragment rather than a fixed molecule. The body keeps glucose in the blood within a narrow range and stores the rest as glycogen in the liver and muscle, unpacking it when the level drops. Branching is the point: a branched chain has many free ends, so many enzymes can strip glucose off at once and release it quickly. Muscle glycogen is only available to that muscle, while liver glycogen is released into the blood for the whole body. Carb-loading before an endurance event is about filling those stores rather than about eating any particular sugar.

glycerol-vs-propylene-glycol.text: Both are viscous, sweet-tasting alcohols used to hold water in a product, and glycerol has one more hydroxyl group, C3H8O3 against C3H8O2. That extra group makes glycerol thicker and more strongly humectant, which is why it dominates in skincare, toothpaste and food glazes. Propylene glycol is thinner and a better solvent for flavour compounds, which is why it carries the flavour in e-liquid and in many oral medicines while glycerol supplies the visible vapour. Glycerol is also a real metabolic molecule: it is the backbone every triglyceride is built on, so the body has an established route for it. Both are widely permitted in food.

hydrochlorothiazide-vs-furosemide.text: Both are diuretics and they act on different parts of the kidney's tubule, which decides how strong each is. Furosemide is a loop diuretic, blocking sodium reabsorption in the thick ascending limb where the bulk of it happens, so it produces a large and fast urine output and is used for fluid overload in heart failure. Hydrochlorothiazide acts further along in the distal tubule, where much less sodium is available to block, so it is gentler and is used for ongoing blood pressure control. They also differ on calcium: thiazides retain it and loop diuretics lose it, which matters for bone and for kidney stones. Furosemide is the heavier at 330.7 against 297.7 and both carry a sulfonamide group.

hydrogen-peroxide-vs-isopropyl-alcohol.text: Both sit in the same first-aid cabinet and they kill microbes by different mechanisms. Hydrogen peroxide is an oxidiser: it breaks down into water and oxygen, and the fizzing on a cut is that reaction being catalysed by an enzyme in your own tissue. Isopropyl alcohol denatures proteins and dissolves membranes instead, which is faster and does not depend on contact with tissue enzymes. Peroxide is the milder disinfectant of the two at the 3 percent strength sold for household use, and it also damages healthy cells in a wound, which is why its use on open cuts has fallen out of favour. Alcohol evaporates and leaves nothing behind; peroxide leaves water.

hydrogen-peroxide-vs-sodium-hypochlorite.text: Both are oxidising bleaches and both are sold for household cleaning, and they leave very different residues. Hydrogen peroxide decomposes into water and oxygen and nothing else, which is why it is the one used on fabric and hair where a chlorine smell would be unwelcome. Sodium hypochlorite releases hypochlorous acid in water, which is the active destroyer of stain pigments and microbial proteins, and it leaves salt behind. Bleach is much the stronger disinfectant at ordinary household concentrations. The important practical difference is not on either page alone: bleach mixed with ammonia or with acid releases toxic gases, and peroxide does not do that.

hydroxyzine-vs-diphenhydramine.text: Both are first generation antihistamines that cross into the brain and cause drowsiness, and they are used for noticeably different things. Diphenhydramine is an over-the-counter allergy medicine and sleep aid with a short duration, a few hours. Hydroxyzine lasts much longer, is prescription-only in most countries, and is used for anxiety and itching as well as allergy, partly because it also acts on serotonin receptors. Hydroxyzine is the heavier molecule at 374.9 against 255.35 and carries a piperazine ring where diphenhydramine has a simple dimethylamine. Cetirizine, the common non-drowsy antihistamine, is actually hydroxyzine's own metabolite with that ring capped by a carboxylic acid.

ibuprofen-vs-naproxen.text: These are the closest pair on the OTC shelf: both NSAIDs, both propionic acid derivatives, both blocking COX. The practical difference is time. Ibuprofen has a half-life near 2 hours and naproxen near 14, which is why one is taken through the day and the other is sold as a twice-daily tablet under the name Aleve. Naproxen is the heavier molecule at 230.26 against 206.28 and carries an extra ether group on a naphthalene ring rather than ibuprofen's simple benzene. Reported oral LD50 sits at 636 mg/kg in rats for ibuprofen and 1234 mg/kg in mice for naproxen, measured in different species, so the two numbers are not directly comparable.

insulin-vs-glucagon.text: These are the two halves of blood sugar control and they are released by neighbouring cells in the same organ. Insulin comes from the beta cells of the pancreas when blood glucose rises, and it tells muscle, fat and liver to take glucose out of the blood and store it. Glucagon comes from the alpha cells when glucose falls, and it tells the liver to break glycogen back down and release it. Both are peptide hormones rather than small molecules, which is why neither survives the stomach and both are injected rather than swallowed. Insulin is much the larger of the two, 51 amino acids in two chains against glucagon's single chain of 29.

isotretinoin-vs-tretinoin.text: These two have the identical formula, C20H28O2, and identical weight, and they differ only in the geometry of one double bond. Tretinoin is all-trans retinoic acid, the natural active form of vitamin A, used topically for acne and photoaging and given systemically for one type of leukaemia. Isotretinoin is the 13-cis isomer, used by mouth for severe acne, where it shrinks sebaceous glands in a way topical retinoids do not. Both are potent teratogens, which is why isotretinoin is dispensed under strict pregnancy-prevention programmes in the US and Europe. That is the practical meaning of the pair: the same atoms, one bond flipped, and two very different regulatory regimes.

lactose-vs-galactose.text: Lactose is milk sugar and galactose is one of its two halves, so this pair is a molecule and its component rather than two competitors. Lactose is glucose joined to galactose at 342.3; splitting it needs the enzyme lactase, and most adults worldwide stop making enough lactase after childhood, which is what lactose intolerance is. Galactose alone is 180.16 and has the same formula as glucose, differing only in the orientation of one hydroxyl group. Babies handle both easily, and a rare inherited inability to process galactose is screened for at birth in many countries. Neither is especially sweet: lactose is one of the least sweet common sugars, which is why milk does not taste sugary.

leptin-vs-ghrelin.text: These two are usually introduced as the fullness hormone and the hunger hormone, and the neat symmetry hides how differently they behave. Ghrelin is made mostly in the stomach, rises before a meal and falls after it, and acts on a timescale of hours: it is a short-term signal to eat now. Leptin is made by fat tissue in proportion to how much of it there is, so it is a long-term signal about energy stores rather than about the next meal. That asymmetry is why the two are not a simple on and off pair. Both are peptide hormones, ghrelin a short chain and leptin a protein several times its size, so neither survives the stomach.

levocetirizine-vs-cetirizine.text: Cetirizine is a mixture of two mirror-image forms of the same molecule, and levocetirizine is just one of them isolated. The active half is levocetirizine, and the other half contributes very little H1 blocking, which is why levocetirizine works at about half the amount of cetirizine for a similar effect. Everything else about them is identical: same formula, same weight of 388.9, same receptor, same once-daily pattern. Whether isolating the active half produces a meaningfully better medicine or mainly a new patent is a debate that has followed several single-isomer products. Cetirizine is generally sold over the counter and levocetirizine varies by country.

limonene-vs-linalool.text: Both are terpenes that carry a scent and both turn up on cosmetic ingredient lists as declared allergens. Limonene is a cyclic hydrocarbon, C10H16, and is the whole of citrus peel oil, which is why it is the solvent in orange-oil cleaners as well as a fragrance. Linalool carries an alcohol group, C10H18O, and is the floral, slightly spicy note in lavender, coriander and basil. That single oxygen makes linalool the less volatile and the more soluble of the two. Both oxidise on exposure to air into products that are more sensitising than the fresh molecules, which is why an old bottle of citrus oil is more likely to irritate skin than a new one.

lisdexamfetamine-vs-dextroamphetamine.text: Lisdexamfetamine is dextroamphetamine with the amino acid lysine attached, and it does nothing at all until enzymes in the blood cut that lysine off. That conversion is the entire design: it happens at a rate the body sets rather than one a formulation sets, which gives a smoother rise and makes the molecule far less useful if crushed or injected. Once cleaved, what circulates is dextroamphetamine, so the two are the same drug arriving by different routes. Lisdexamfetamine is the much heavier molecule at 263.38 against 135.21 because of the attached lysine, and only part of that weight is the active portion. Both are controlled substances in the US.

lisinopril-vs-losartan.text: Both lower blood pressure by interrupting the same hormone system at different points. Lisinopril is an ACE inhibitor: it blocks the enzyme that converts angiotensin I into angiotensin II, so less of the vessel-tightening hormone is made. Losartan is an angiotensin receptor blocker: the hormone is still made but cannot act on its receptor. That difference explains the best-known side effect split, because ACE also breaks down bradykinin, and the bradykinin that accumulates under lisinopril causes the persistent dry cough that losartan does not. Losartan is much the heavier molecule at 422.9 against 405.5 and carries a tetrazole ring. Both are prescription medicines.

loratadine-vs-cetirizine.text: Both are second generation antihistamines taken once a day and both block the H1 receptor. Cetirizine crosses into the brain slightly more than loratadine does, so it is a little more likely to cause drowsiness while also tending to act faster and more strongly on symptoms. Loratadine is a prodrug in effect: the liver converts much of it to desloratadine, which is what does most of the work, and that adds a step cetirizine does not have. Cetirizine is the heavier molecule at 388.9 against 382.9 and carries a carboxylic acid where loratadine carries a carbamate ester. Both are sold over the counter in most countries.

loratadine-vs-diphenhydramine.text: This is the Claritin and Benadryl comparison, and it is the clearest example of what separates antihistamine generations. Diphenhydramine is a small, fat-soluble first generation molecule that crosses into the brain easily, which is why it works within an hour and reliably causes drowsiness, and why it doubles as a sleep aid. Loratadine is built to stay out of the brain, so it is non-sedating for most people, but it lasts a full day where diphenhydramine's effect fades in a few hours. Diphenhydramine also blocks acetylcholine receptors, which is where the dry mouth and blurred vision come from, and loratadine largely does not. Loratadine is much the heavier molecule at 382.9 against 255.35.

losartan-vs-valsartan.text: Both are angiotensin receptor blockers that keep angiotensin II from acting on its receptor, and they differ mainly in pharmacokinetics. Losartan is a prodrug in part: the liver converts some of it into a metabolite that is considerably more active than the parent, so its effect depends on that conversion. Valsartan is active as given. Losartan also has a mild uric-acid lowering effect that the rest of the class does not share, which is a genuinely distinctive property. Valsartan is the heavier at 435.5 against 422.9 and carries a carboxylic acid where losartan carries an alcohol. Both are prescription medicines and both belong to a class that came out of a large recall over nitrosamine contamination in the late 2010s.

lutein-vs-zeaxanthin.text: These two are isomers of each other, the same C40H56O2 formula with one double bond in a different position, and they are the only carotenoids the eye concentrates in the macula. That single bond changes how each orients in the retina: zeaxanthin sits at the very centre of the macula and lutein spreads more toward the periphery. Both absorb blue light and both are antioxidants, which is the basis of the interest in them for eye health. Dietary sources differ, with lutein highest in kale, spinach and other dark greens and zeaxanthin higher in corn, orange peppers and egg yolk. The body can convert lutein into a form of zeaxanthin, which is why supplements usually pair them.

lycopene-vs-beta-carotene.text: These two carotenoids have the identical formula, C40H56, and identical weight, and they differ only in that beta-carotene closes rings at both ends while lycopene stays open. That ring is what makes beta-carotene a vitamin A precursor and lycopene not one: the body cuts the molecule at its centre and needs the ring to make retinol. Colour follows the same structural difference, lycopene reading red in tomato and watermelon and beta-carotene orange in carrot. Both are fat soluble, so both are absorbed better with oil, and lycopene is unusual in becoming more available after cooking, which is why processed tomato products carry more usable lycopene than raw tomatoes.

maltodextrin-vs-starch.text: Maltodextrin is starch that has been partly taken apart, so this pair is a material and its own fragment. Starch is long chains of glucose, either straight amylose or branched amylopectin, and it needs digestion before the body can use it. Maltodextrin is the same glucose chains cut down to a few units, which makes it dissolve instantly, taste faintly sweet where starch tastes of nothing, and raise blood glucose faster than table sugar does. That combination is why it is everywhere in sports drinks, powdered foods and seasoning blends: it carries flavour, adds body, and dissolves without lumping. Starch is the storage form plants actually make; maltodextrin is an industrial product.

melatonin-vs-serotonin.text: Melatonin is made from serotonin in two enzymatic steps, so one is the raw material for the other rather than an alternative to it. The pineal gland runs that conversion in darkness, which is why melatonin is the body's nightfall signal and why light at night suppresses it. Serotonin's role is broader and mostly daytime and mostly not in the brain at all: around ninety percent of the body's serotonin is in the gut. The structures show the two added groups, an acetyl on the nitrogen and a methyl on the oxygen, which take serotonin's 176.21 to melatonin's 232.28. Melatonin is sold over the counter in the US and is prescription-only in much of Europe, while serotonin is not sold as a supplement at all because it does not cross into the brain from the bloodstream.

melatonin-vs-zolpidem.text: Both are used for sleep and they are not the same kind of thing at all. Melatonin is a hormone the body produces in darkness, a signal that says night has come rather than a sedative, and it is sold over the counter in the US while being prescription-only in much of Europe. Zolpidem is a prescription sedative that acts on the GABA-A receptor, the same target as the benzodiazepines, and it induces sleep directly. That mechanistic difference shows in what each does to sleep architecture and in the risks attached: zolpidem carries well-documented associations with complex sleep behaviours and next-day impairment, melatonin does not. Melatonin's own half-life is very short at around 45 minutes.

meloxicam-vs-ibuprofen.text: Meloxicam is an NSAID like ibuprofen but leans toward COX-2, and it is dosed once a day where ibuprofen is dosed through the day, because it lingers far longer in the body. The structures are not close: meloxicam is an oxicam built on a thiazine ring with a sulfur-containing core, while ibuprofen is a small propionic acid on a benzene ring, and the weights differ accordingly at 351.4 against 206.28. Meloxicam is prescription only in most countries and ibuprofen is not, which is the practical line between them. Both carry the class effects NSAIDs share, on the stomach lining and on the kidneys, and neither selectivity nor dosing schedule removes those.

menthol-vs-camphor.text: Both are terpenoids that produce a sensation the body reads as temperature, and they trip different receptors. Menthol activates TRPM8, the cold receptor, which is why it feels cool without lowering any temperature, and it is the reason peppermint and menthol cigarettes feel the way they do. Camphor is less selective, working on several TRP channels including the warm ones, which is why it reads as both cooling and warming and why it appears in chest rubs alongside menthol rather than instead of it. Camphor is the more toxic of the two by a wide margin and is dangerous to children if swallowed, which is why its concentration in consumer products is capped in many countries. Menthol comes from mint, camphor from the camphor laurel or from synthesis.

metformin-vs-semaglutide.text: These are both treatments for type 2 diabetes and they are barely comparable as molecules. Metformin is tiny, four carbons and five nitrogens at 129.16, descended from a compound in goat's rue, and it works mainly by reducing glucose production in the liver and improving insulin sensitivity. Semaglutide is a peptide of 31 amino acids at 4114, a modified copy of the gut hormone GLP-1 with a fatty acid chain attached so it binds albumin and lasts a week rather than minutes. Semaglutide slows stomach emptying and acts on appetite centres, which is why it also produces substantial weight loss, and metformin does so only slightly. Metformin is taken by mouth and remains the usual first-line choice; semaglutide is normally injected, with one oral formulation.

methane-vs-propane.text: Both are alkanes burned as fuel and only one of them can be practically bottled. Methane is the simplest hydrocarbon, CH4, and boils at about minus 162 degrees Celsius, so keeping it liquid needs cryogenic equipment and mains gas is delivered as a gas through pipes instead. Propane liquefies under modest pressure at ordinary temperatures, which is why a barbecue bottle can hold days of fuel in a few kilograms. Propane also carries more energy per unit volume, so a burner designed for one will not run correctly on the other without a jet change. Methane is much the lighter at 16.04 against 44.1 and rises when it leaks; propane is heavier than air and pools, which is a real difference in how a leak behaves.

methylphenidate-vs-amphetamine.text: These are the two stimulant families used for ADHD, sold as Ritalin and as Adderall, and they move dopamine by different mechanisms. Methylphenidate blocks the dopamine and norepinephrine transporters, so it stops reuptake and lets naturally released neurotransmitter linger. Amphetamine does that too and goes further: it enters the neuron and forces stored dopamine out through the transporter running in reverse, so it increases release rather than only preserving it. That extra step is why amphetamine tends to produce a stronger effect and why its abuse potential is generally rated higher. Methylphenidate is the heavier molecule at 233.31 against 135.21, and both are controlled substances.

metoprolol-vs-propranolol.text: Both are beta blockers and the difference is selectivity. Propranolol blocks beta-1 and beta-2 receptors alike, so alongside slowing the heart it also acts on airway and peripheral vessels, which is why it is used for tremor, migraine prevention and performance anxiety and why it is avoided in asthma. Metoprolol is relatively beta-1 selective, aiming at the heart and leaving the airways comparatively alone, though that selectivity fades at higher amounts. Propranolol is also far more fat-soluble, so it enters the brain readily, which is part of why it has a role in anxiety that metoprolol largely lacks. Metoprolol is the heavier at 267.36 against 259.34.

monosodium-glutamate-vs-sodium-chloride.text: Both are sodium salts that a cook reaches for, and they trigger different taste receptors. Sodium chloride is read as salty by ion channels responding to the sodium itself; monosodium glutamate is read as umami by a receptor that detects the glutamate half, and the sodium is incidental. MSG carries roughly a third of the sodium of table salt for the same weight, since most of its mass is the glutamate. Glutamate is one of the twenty standard amino acids and is present naturally in tomatoes, parmesan, soy sauce and mushrooms, so the taste is not novel even where the ingredient is. The reported oral LD50 for table salt is 3000 mg/kg in rats, higher than several substances people treat with more caution.

morphine-vs-fentanyl.text: Both bind the same target, the mu-opioid receptor, and the enormous difference between them is how tightly and how easily they get there. Morphine is the natural alkaloid isolated from opium poppy in 1804, a rigid five-ring structure with two hydroxyl groups that make it relatively water-loving and slow to cross into the brain. Fentanyl is fully synthetic, much smaller in ring count, and far more fat-soluble, so it reaches the brain in minutes and acts at a small fraction of the amount. The reported oral LD50 values sit at 335 mg/kg in rats for morphine and 18 mg/kg in rats for fentanyl, a ratio that understates the difference in potency at ordinary exposures. That potency gap is the reason fentanyl dominates overdose statistics: the margin between a working amount and a fatal one is measured in units a kitchen scale cannot see.

naloxone-vs-naltrexone.text: These two are constantly confused, they differ by one small chemical group, and what they are used for could hardly be less alike. Both are opioid antagonists: they occupy the mu-opioid receptor and switch nothing on, which displaces any opioid already there. Naloxone is poorly absorbed by mouth and acts within minutes when injected or sprayed into the nose, which is why it is the overdose reversal agent carried in emergency kits. Naltrexone survives the gut, lasts many hours, and is used to maintain a blocked receptor over time rather than to rescue anyone in an emergency. The structural difference is an allyl group on naloxone against a cyclopropylmethyl group on naltrexone, and the weights are 327.4 and 341.4.

nicotinamide-vs-niacin.text: Both are vitamin B3 and both end up as the same coenzyme, NAD, but they behave very differently on the way there. Niacin is nicotinic acid, carrying a carboxylic acid group, and at high intakes it causes the flush, a temporary reddening and prickling of the skin driven by prostaglandin release. Nicotinamide carries an amide instead and does not cause the flush at all, which is why supplements sold as flush-free use it. That same carboxylic acid is why niacin, and not nicotinamide, has effects on blood lipids. In skincare the amide form is the one used, listed as niacinamide, where it is studied for barrier function and pigmentation.

nicotine-vs-caffeine.text: Both are plant alkaloids that plants make to poison insects, and both are stimulants in people, but they act on completely different receptors. Nicotine binds acetylcholine receptors directly; caffeine works by blocking adenosine, the molecule that builds up while you are awake and makes you feel sleepy. The habit-forming pull is not comparable: nicotine is one of the most reinforcing drugs known, and caffeine produces a mild dependence that shows up mostly as a headache when it stops. Nicotine also clears far faster, a half-life near 2 hours against caffeine's 5, which is part of why smoking is paced in minutes and coffee in hours. Their oral LD50 values in rats are almost identical at 188 and 192 mg/kg, which says nothing useful about how each is actually encountered.

oleic-acid-vs-linoleic-acid.text: Both are eighteen-carbon fatty acids and the difference is one double bond, C18H34O2 against C18H32O2. Oleic acid has a single cis double bond and is monounsaturated; linoleic acid has two and is the parent of the omega-6 family. That second bond makes linoleic acid more prone to oxidation, which is why sunflower and corn oil go rancid faster than olive oil and why olive oil keeps longer on a shelf and holds up to moderate heat. Linoleic acid is essential: the human body cannot introduce a double bond that far along the chain, so it must come from food, while oleic acid the body makes for itself. Oleic acid is most of olive oil and is why it stays liquid in a fridge where butter does not.

oxycodone-vs-hydrocodone.text: These two are close enough that people mix them up routinely, and structurally they nearly are the same molecule: both semi-synthetic opioids built from thebaine, differing by a single hydroxyl group that oxycodone carries and hydrocodone does not. Both bind the mu-opioid receptor, both are prescription painkillers, and both are controlled in the US and elsewhere. Hydrocodone is very often sold combined with acetaminophen, which oxycodone sometimes is and sometimes is not, and that combination is the reason a hydrocodone product carries a second drug's limits along with its own. The weights differ by the oxygen alone, 315.4 against 299.4. Both entries here carry the same GHS hazard framing and the same prescription-medicine bucket.

oxytocin-vs-vasopressin.text: These two are so similar that they are almost the same molecule: nine amino acids each, differing at only two positions, and both released from the posterior pituitary. That near-identity means each has some activity at the other's receptors, which is one reason their effects are hard to separate cleanly in studies. Oxytocin drives uterine contraction and milk letdown and is the one that gets written about for social bonding. Vasopressin, also called antidiuretic hormone, tells the kidney to reclaim water and constricts blood vessels, so it is the one that governs how concentrated your urine is. Both are peptides, so neither is absorbed usefully from the gut.

palmitic-acid-vs-stearic-acid.text: Both are saturated fatty acids with no double bonds at all, and they differ by two carbons, C16H32O2 against C18H36O2. That length difference raises stearic acid's melting point, which is why it is the one that gives a candle and a bar of soap their body and why cocoa butter is solid at room temperature and melts in the mouth. Palmitic acid is the most common saturated fat in the food supply and in human tissue, and is the one the body makes first when it synthesises fat. Their metabolic reputations differ: stearic acid is largely converted to oleic acid in the liver and has little effect on blood cholesterol, while palmitic acid raises LDL, which is unusual for two molecules so nearly identical.

prednisone-vs-dexamethasone.text: Both are corticosteroids that suppress inflammation through the glucocorticoid receptor, and dexamethasone is several times the more potent per unit weight. Prednisone is inactive as swallowed and must be converted by the liver into prednisolone, which dexamethasone does not require. They also differ in mineralocorticoid effect: prednisone retains some, so it holds sodium and water more than dexamethasone, which has essentially none, and that is why dexamethasone is preferred where fluid retention is a problem. Dexamethasone lasts far longer, with a biological effect measured in a day and a half against prednisone's half day. Dexamethasone carries a fluorine that prednisone lacks, at 392.5 against 358.4.

quercetin-vs-epigallocatechin-gallate.text: Both are plant polyphenols with antioxidant reputations and they come from different chemical families. Quercetin is a flavonol with a flat, conjugated three-ring core and five hydroxyl groups, widespread in onions, apples, capers and tea. Epigallocatechin gallate is a flavan-3-ol from green tea specifically, much larger at 458.4 against 302.2, and its extra gallate ester is what makes it the most studied compound in green tea. EGCG is also the more unstable of the two, oxidising readily in warm water and in the gut, which complicates dose comparisons between studies. Both bind proteins and metal ions readily, which is part of why both interfere with the absorption of iron from a meal.

quercetin-vs-resveratrol.text: Both are plant polyphenols sold as antioxidant supplements and they belong to different classes. Quercetin is a flavonoid, a three-ring structure with five hydroxyl groups, and it is one of the most abundant flavonoids in the ordinary diet, concentrated in onion skin, capers, apples and tea. Resveratrol is a much simpler stilbene, two rings joined by a double bond, found in grape skin, red wine and Japanese knotweed, and it became famous through the French paradox. Both are poorly absorbed and rapidly conjugated by the liver, which is the central difficulty in translating their laboratory activity into anything measured in people. Quercetin is the heavier at 302.2 against 228.24.

quetiapine-vs-olanzapine.text: Both are atypical antipsychotics that block dopamine D2 and serotonin 5-HT2A receptors, and they differ most in how tightly they hold on. Quetiapine binds D2 loosely and comes off quickly, which is why it causes relatively few movement side effects and why it is heavily sedating at lower amounts through its antihistamine activity. Olanzapine binds more firmly and is the more reliably antipsychotic of the two, at the cost of a stronger association with weight gain and metabolic change. Both carry sedation, and both are prescription only. Quetiapine is a dibenzothiazepine at 383.5 and olanzapine a thienobenzodiazepine at 312.4, so they are structural cousins rather than the same skeleton.

semaglutide-vs-tirzepatide.text: Both are injectable peptides that copy gut hormones, and tirzepatide targets one receptor more than semaglutide does. Semaglutide is a GLP-1 receptor agonist; tirzepatide is a dual agonist, hitting both GIP and GLP-1 receptors, which is the basis for the larger average weight loss reported in head-to-head trials. Both carry a fatty acid chain that binds albumin and stretches their action to about a week. They are the two largest molecules in this catalog by a wide margin, semaglutide at 4114 and tirzepatide at 4813, so both are chains rather than small molecules and neither survives the stomach in its ordinary form. Semaglutide is sold as Ozempic and Wegovy, tirzepatide as Mounjaro and Zepbound.

serotonin-vs-dopamine.text: Both are monoamine neurotransmitters built from an amino acid, dopamine from tyrosine and serotonin from tryptophan, and both are routinely oversimplified in popular writing. Dopamine is most associated with motivation and the anticipation of reward, the wanting rather than the liking, and it is also central to movement, which is what Parkinson's disease depletes. Serotonin is spread more widely still, with the large majority of the body's supply in the gut rather than the brain, where it regulates motility. Neither is a happiness molecule, and the calling of one the reward chemical and the other the happiness chemical does not survive contact with the pharmacology. Serotonin is also the direct precursor the body converts into melatonin at night.

sertraline-vs-escitalopram.text: These are the two most prescribed SSRIs and both block the serotonin transporter, but escitalopram is the more selective of the two by a wide margin. Sertraline also has meaningful activity at the dopamine transporter and at sigma receptors, which escitalopram essentially lacks. Escitalopram is the isolated active half of citalopram, so it is a single-isomer molecule where sertraline is not, and it is the heavier at 324.4 against 306.2. In practice their side effect profiles overlap heavily and differ in the details. Both are prescription medicines and neither is available over the counter anywhere in the US or Europe.

sertraline-vs-fluoxetine.text: Both are SSRIs, both block the serotonin transporter, and the practical difference between them is how long they stay. Fluoxetine carries a trifluoromethyl group and produces an active metabolite, norfluoxetine, that persists for a week or more, so its level falls very slowly when it stops. Sertraline carries two chlorines on a naphthalene core instead and clears in a day or two. That difference shapes how each behaves at the edges: fluoxetine is the more forgiving of a missed dose and the harder to stop cleanly, sertraline the reverse. Fluoxetine was the first SSRI to reach the market, in 1987 as Prozac, and sertraline followed as Zoloft and is now among the most prescribed medicines in the world.

sildenafil-vs-tadalafil.text: Both are PDE5 inhibitors, keeping cyclic GMP from being broken down so blood vessels stay relaxed, and the difference that matters is duration. Sildenafil acts for roughly four to six hours; tadalafil's half-life is around 17.5 hours and its effect can span a day and a half, which is why it acquired the weekend nickname. Sildenafil is the more affected by a fatty meal, which slows its absorption, and tadalafil much less so. Their side effect profiles follow their off-target selectivity: sildenafil has some activity at PDE6 in the retina, which produces the occasional blue tinge to vision, while tadalafil has more at PDE11, which is associated with back and muscle ache. Both were developed for cardiovascular indications before their current ones and both remain in use for pulmonary hypertension.

sodium-bicarbonate-vs-sodium-carbonate.text: Baking soda and washing soda are the same two elements in different proportions, NaHCO3 against Na2CO3, and the extra sodium makes all the difference to how alkaline they are. Sodium bicarbonate is mildly alkaline and safe to eat, which is why it leavens cake and settles indigestion. Sodium carbonate is strongly alkaline, will irritate skin, and is used to soften laundry water and cut grease. Heating baking soda in an oven converts it into washing soda, releasing carbon dioxide and water, which is the same reaction that raises a cake. In baking, the carbon dioxide is the point; in cleaning, the alkalinity is.

sodium-chloride-vs-potassium-chloride.text: Both are simple salts of chloride and both taste salty, and only sodium chloride tastes purely so. Potassium chloride is the main ingredient in the salt substitutes sold as NoSalt and LoSalt, and it carries a metallic, faintly bitter edge that gets stronger with concentration, which is why substitutes are usually blends rather than straight potassium chloride. The saltiness is read by different mechanisms: the sodium ion passes through an ion channel on the taste cell directly, and the potassium ion is a poorer fit for it. The reported oral LD50 values differ sharply, 3000 mg/kg in rats for table salt against 383 mg/kg in mice for potassium chloride, measured in different species but pointing at a real difference: potassium load matters to the heart in a way sodium load does not.

sodium-hydroxide-vs-sodium-bicarbonate.text: Both are alkaline and they sit at opposite ends of that scale. Sodium bicarbonate is weak enough to eat and is used to neutralise acid in a stomach or a recipe. Sodium hydroxide is caustic soda, strong enough to saponify fat and dissolve hair, which is what makes it the active ingredient in drain cleaner and in soap making. The GHS classifications say it plainly: sodium hydroxide carries the corrosive pictogram and bicarbonate does not. Weights are close at 40.0 and 84.01, which is a reminder that molecular size says nothing about hazard. Sodium hydroxide releases significant heat when it dissolves, and bicarbonate does not.

starch-vs-cellulose.text: Both are long chains of glucose and nothing else, and a single bond orientation decides whether you can eat them. Starch links its glucose units with alpha bonds, which human amylase can cut, so starch is food. Cellulose links them with beta bonds, which flips every second unit over and produces a flat ribbon that human enzymes cannot touch, so cellulose is dietary fibre. Those flat ribbons stack and hydrogen-bond into fibres, which is why cellulose is structural in plants and starch is not: one is the plant's warehouse and the other is its scaffolding. Cows and termites manage cellulose only by hosting microbes that carry the missing enzyme.

stevioside-vs-rebaudioside-a.text: These two come out of the same stevia leaf and differ by one sugar unit, which is why rebaudioside A is the heavier molecule at 967.0 against 804.9. Both are steviol glycosides: the same steviol core with different sugars hung off it. Stevioside is the more abundant compound in the raw leaf and around 200 times as sweet as sugar, but it carries a liquorice bitterness in the finish. Rebaudioside A is the cleaner tasting of the two and slightly sweeter, near 250 times sugar, which is why most commercial stevia products are purified toward it.
